t.1.23.1: The Sūta said: Being carried by Suparṇa, they swiftly went to that region, which was encircled by the waters of the ocean and resounded with flocks of birds.
t.1.23.2: It was surrounded by rows of forest trees bearing many-hued fruits and flowers, and it was likewise surrounded by charming dwellings and by lotus ponds as well.
t.1.23.3: It was adorned with wonderful lakes of clear water, and fanned by holy breezes carrying heavenly fragrances.
t.1.23.4: It was adorned also by trees born on Malaya, which seemed to kiss the sky and which, shaken by the wind, let fall showers of flowers.
t.1.23.6: Having reached that forest, the serpents sported there with delight, and they spoke to Suparṇa, the mighty one, the best of birds.
t.1.23.5: With its trees seeming to scatter showers of flowers and water upon the Nāgas standing there, the forest was holy and gladdening to the mind, dear to the Gandharvas and Apsarases. It was lovely, filled with the cries of many kinds of birds, and a delight to the sons of Kadrū.
t.1.23.7: Carry us to another island, very delightful and abounding in water; for you, O sky-rover, see many delightful lands as you fly.
t.1.23.8: Then the bird, having reflected, said to his mother Vinatā: "For what reason, mother, must I do what the serpents have spoken?"
t.1.23.9: O best of birds, I have become the slave of my ignoble sister, having entered into a false wager that was rigged by the serpents through trickery.
t.1.23.10: When that reason had been told by his mother, the sky-goer, pained by that sorrow, spoke these words to the serpents.
t.1.23.11: By bringing what, or by learning what, or by performing what feat of valor here, might I be released from bondage to you? Tell me the truth, O serpents!
t.1.23.12: Having heard him, the serpents said: “Bring the amṛta by your might; then there will be release from slavery for you, O sky-ranger.”
